speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history of bone fragility. To understand your condition better, can you describe the specific unusual physical features you have noticed?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency). The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth (clitoromegaly, labial fusion), history of fractures (suggesting bone density issues from chronic cortisol/corticoid imbalance), and maternal hirsutism during pregnancy strongly points to a classic form of CAH with a late diagnosis due to the patient being female. I recommend immediate testing of 17-hydroxyprogesterone levels to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: 17-hydroxyprogesterone
